root_cause_label: Inadequate Regex Strategy for State-Space Expansion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never grasped that sequential regex substitutions over a single string cannot enumerate multiple legal chess positions; its pawn-move patterns (and subsequent piece-move patterns) performed single-string in-place edits rather than cloning the board state once per candidate move, so the output never exceeded 2 entries and was always malformed.
t_err_evidence: Step 17 is the first attempt at move-generation logic; the agent writes pawn-move rules such as 'P(.{8})' -> '.P\1' that perform a single in-place substitution on one string instead of emitting N copies of the board—one per legal move. This fundamental design flaw (single-string mutation vs. multi-copy generation) means no correct multi-move output can ever be produced by this strategy.
t_commit_evidence: From step 17 onward the agent iterates exclusively on variants of the same flawed single-string substitution approach—adjusting escaping, re-ordering rules, trying generator scripts, focusing on individual piece types—but never considers a fundamentally different strategy. By step 17 the wrong design is locked in and all subsequent work is incremental patching of an inherently broken method.
t_surface_evidence: Step 18 is the first test run after the move-generation logic is written; it immediately fails with a JSONDecodeError caused by invalid escape sequences in the newly written rules, making the approach visibly broken. By step 20 the logic produces 2 moves (one empty string) vs. 20 expected, confirming the strategy is fundamentally incorrect.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain knowledge that regex-based chess move generation requires cloning the entire board string once per candidate move (producing N newline-separated copies) rather than making a single in-place substitution. It designs all its patterns around the latter, incorrect model, and every subsequent iteration inherits this misconception.
forewarning_evidence: Step 16 shows the initial (expansion-only) re.json produces 1 move vs 20 expected—already signaling that the approach to expanding and then enumerating moves is not generating the right number of outputs. The agent acknowledges this but attributes it to missing move-generation logic rather than a structural problem with the single-string approach.
